previousIssues.issue: w8a/w8b MEDIUM: welcome-galley pane opaque, diagonal sheen strip reads as a plank
previousIssues.status: partly fixed. The tilted sheen strip is gone (m03, m16, m14) and the pane is lighter: #4d4742 at m03 (660,250) and #4b4540 at (660,350), against lalf_134 #605154 / #614d4f. However, the pane is still an opaque quad, so the lit boxes behind it (#8d8a84, #b0aca4) never show. The three #3a3835 shadow lines read as glazing bars, so the cabinet looks like a panelled taupe door with muntins rather than smoked glass. In lalf_134 (910-1010, 300-760) and omaat_room_32 (740-900, 180-700), a white-ish interior, a shelf and a red object are plainly visible through the pane.

previousIssues.issue: w8b MEDIUM: F front drape hangs as a free column in mid-passage
previousIssues.status: fixed. m02 shows the drape bunched against the edge of the ink-cloud centre wall (x 515-625). q01 shows it against the left ebony jamb (x 385-500), with no gap on the jamb side. This now reads like omaatF_40, where the drape hangs at the wall edge under the EXIT sign.

previousIssues.issue: w7b HIGH / w7a MEDIUM: Type A door-lining furniture mirrored fore-aft
previousIssues.status: fixed and still holds (m18, m17, m13). The arming window is upper aft and the arc runs over the top to a down-pointing arrowhead on the forward side. The grip, assist bar and crimson strap are on the aft half. The cream EXIT plate (w8a) now sits above the housing, as in lalf_133.

previousIssues.issue: w7a/w7b MEDIUM: welcome-galley glass door had no pane, frame or boss
previousIssues.status: fixed for frame, boss and tag. See the pane item above for the remaining see-through problem.

previousIssues.issue: w7b: door-3 bar blind was a featureless black void
previousIssues.status: partly regressed, probably from the lighting snapshots 282136c / 9f2d20e. In m05 the blind samples #09090a (350,200) and #070708 (350,300), with only faint slat lines. It is greyer in m06 and q11. The ANA render's black panel is #1c1b23 / #18171c, so it now renders darker than the reference, although this is still a black-panel product. Low.

previousIssues.issue: w8b LOW: faint vertical seam in the lower middle ash flap
previousIssues.status: not fixed. It is still faintly visible at m04 x~465, y 490-575 (#c8bca2 against #c5b89e beside it).

previousIssues.issue: w8b LOW: welcome counter reads mid-grey, not glossy black

details.note: The layout matches samchui_render_11: black back panel, landscape monitor, glass fridge with oval latch, bottle cubby, black counter with chrome nosing, ash lower doors with round pulls, black soffit with three downlights. The bottles are cones with no neck or shoulder and read as grey shells. The blind is darker than the render. There is still no in-service photo.

Monitor, ovens, control panel, ash lower doors, aluminium nosing and the round boss are right. The pane still does not read as glass. The tower recess and the bays under the monitor render near-black (#1a1917, #161513) instead of lit dark bronze. The brewer reads as a dark slate box (#434952), not silver.

The ash wall with aluminium-framed flaps and red latches matches lalf_133. The frames are square-cornered, flat strips where the real ones have rounded corners and a raised bevelled profile with a twin red latch on a silver bracket. The seam is still present.

details.detail: F front wall, flight-deck corridor, door 1 (q01, m02, m19, m01)
details.note: The drape is now at the wall edge. The ebony corridor (#443939 / #483e3e, against tpa_Image-2-3 #433a3b / #44494d) and the cockpit door with its white frames and yellow kick strip are good. The cockpit door's aluminium surround is thinner than the real wide brushed jamb.
Ash J lav doors with white strip, grab and sign, plus white PY/Y lavs. No change.

details.detail: F/J bulkhead, J faces (m07, m14, m15)
details.note: Cream walls, panel seam, blue-topped wall boxes and tied charcoal curtains. The curtain is slightly warm (#49413c at m07 575,400) against omaat_room_36 #39383f, which is cooler.

Charcoal-framed monitors, open gap over the outboard panels and floor pouches all match alv_IMG_7207/7209. The bassinet fitting is drawn as a horizontal steel bar at 1.08 m; alv_IMG_7207 shows only two small round sockets.
The PY aft navy drapes are good. The galley bank is let down by the beverage makers (see the inserts item) and by a strong grey gradient band across the upper units (lighting).
A credible U-galley with drawers, waste flap, trolleys and chunky red latches. It is based on the seat map only. The overhead is a flat white light box (lighting).

details.detail: Standard galley inserts (m01, m09, m12, q19)
details.note: Ovens, standard units, red latches and labels are fine. The beverage makers are wide black blocks with a straight ridged cylinder that reads as a stack of cups. Real ANA units (sans_38, sansY_44) are narrow stainless-framed brewers with a black display strip and a bulbous stainless jug with a black handle.
The F front position is fixed. The J, PY and rear curtains are good. The J charcoal is slightly warm.

details.detail: Jump seats + Type A door linings (m13, m17, m18)
details.note: The lining layout is right. The jump seats render nearly as light as the lining (#a4a4a6 against lining #b7b5b0), whereas in lalf_133 the seat and pedestal are clearly mid-dark grey (#6b6b6d / #575350 against lining #e1cdb2). The grip pocket renders as a black slot; the real one is a light recess around the silver lever.

issues.problem: The folded jump seats and their pedestals render almost as light as the white door lining and monument walls, so they read as part of the wall. In lalf_133 the jump seat and its stowage pedestal are a clearly darker mid grey, about 0.45-0.5 of the lining brightness. In the render the ratio is about 0.9.
issues.evidence: m18 (345,300) #acadae and (340,440) #8c8d8e against lining (520,250) #b6b4af. m13 (255,340) #a4a4a6 against wall (60,240) #b7b5b0. m17 (440,330) #a7a8aa. Reference lalf_133 seat (560,590) #6b6b6d, pedestal (560,700) #575350 / (560,800) #766f67, against lining (650,580) #e1cdb2.
issues.fix: In MONMAT (top of src/10_mono.js): set jump to { c: '#5f5e5c', r: 0.65, l: LAYER.fabric } (was #8a8987) and jumpBase to { c: '#77736d', r: 0.5, l: LAYER.plastic } (was #a3a19d). Keep harness at #5c5f66, or darken it to #3f4247 so the straps still read on the darker cushion.

issues.detail: Galley beverage makers (m01, m09, m12, q19)
issues.problem: Every brewer is a wide black block, about the full unit width, with a straight-sided ridged steel cylinder under it that reads as a stack of cups or plates. The real ANA units are narrow, stainless-framed coffee makers about 0.2 m wide. Each has a black display strip with green keys at the top and a bulbous stainless jug with a black handle in a dark bay. The black mass is the most visible wrong shape in all four galley views.
issues.evidence: m09 brewer at x 0-150 and x 500-670, y 230-410: black #0x block, cylinder (570,370) #3e434c. m01 (285-430, 230-395). sans_38 (660-890, 105-305): stainless units #767362 with jugs. sansY_44 (630-1000, 0-270): bulbous stainless jugs with black handles.
issues.fix: In buildGalley, branch t === 1: make the head and side cheeks MONMAT.aluDark instead of bevBlack, and keep only a black display strip: gRBox(uW, 0.035, 0.01) at y 1.62 in bevBlack, with the green key on it. Keep the bay back bevBlack. Replace gCyl(0.05,0.055,0.13) with a jug lathe: gCyl(0.045,0.06,0.07) at y 1.34, gCyl(0.06,0.04,0.06) at y 1.40, a lid gCyl(0.035,0.035,0.012) at y 1.435, and a handle gRBox(0.015,0.08,0.03) in bevBlack at x+0.065, y 1.37. To split one bay into two jugs like sans_38, loop s in [-uW/4, uW/4] with width uW/2 - 0.02.

issues.detail: Door-2 welcome galley, glass cabinet + tower recess
issues.problem: (a) The pane is still opaque. The lit shelves and boxes behind it never show, and the shelf-shadow lines read as glazing bars, so the cabinet looks like a panelled taupe door rather than smoked glass. (b) The recessed tower face around the monitor and the two bays under it render near-black. In lalf_134 and omaat_room_32 the tower is a lit dark bronze/charcoal with visible frames and lit bay interiors. (c) The 'silver' brewer renders as dark slate.
issues.evidence: (a) m03 pane (660,250) #4d4742. lalf_134 pane (950,700) #605154 and (960,450) #614d4f, with the pale interior, shelf edge and red object visible. (b) m03 tower face (520,180) #1a1917 and bay (530,390) #161513, against lalf_134 tower (1150,350) #5c3818 (warm lit) and omaat_room_32 frame (820,500) #565151. (c) m16 brewer (320,370) #434952, against omaat_room_32's bright silver brewer at x 390-460, y 450-610.
issues.fix: In buildWelcomeGalley: (a) drop the pane quad's diffuse to a thin tint by moving it behind the contents. Put the pane at o+0.03, behind the boxes at o+0.035, and give the boxes and shelves e:0.06 so they read through. Alternatively, keep the pane at o+0.088 but draw it as two narrow sheen strips (0.03 x 0.70, {c:'#7c776f', r:0.05, e:0.06}) at the hinge-side and latch-side edges and leave the centre open. Delete the three gQuad(0.34, 0.012) shadow lines. (b) Add a warm LED strip under the ash head across the opening: gBox(w - 0.1, 0.01, 0.02) at V(0, 1.985, o + 0.3) with { c: '#ffe6c4', e: 0.9 }. Also give welcomeChar e:0.02, or raise its albedo to about #6e685e, because the 0.38 m set-back sits in the head's shadow. (c) Raise the brewer to MONMAT.steelBright and add e:0.03, or this goes to lighting as a recess-fill hand-off.

issues.problem: The bottles are cones without a neck or shoulder, so they read as grey shells. They also lack the white label band seen in the render, where they are clear glass with white labels and blue (water) or amber contents.
issues.evidence: m05 bottles x 625-765, y 320-405 (#3a474d) and fridge bottles (820,230) #404e55. samchui_render_11 (560-650, 260-345): clear bottles with white labels and slim necks.
issues.fix: In bottle(): replace the cone with a shoulder gCyl(r*0.45, r, h*0.12) at h*0.72, then a neck gCyl(r*0.32, r*0.32, h*0.16) at h*0.86 and a cap gCyl(r*0.36, r*0.36, h*0.04) at h*0.96. Use lblMat MONMAT.label for the bar bottles. Lighten bottleClear to #c5d3d6 with e:0.03 so the bottles read as glass under the soffit.

issues.problem: The horizontal pocket behind the silver grip renders as a black slot, which is the most contrasting element on the lining. In lalf_133 the lever sits in a shallow recess only slightly darker than the cream housing.
issues.evidence: m18 slot around (400,365); m17 (600,395) #6c7179 with a black surround. lalf_133 handle recess (620-700, 570-610) is light grey around the silver lever.
issues.fix: In the door-lining block, change the pocket quad gQuad(0.33, 0.14) material from #4a4641 to { c: '#a7a299', r: 0.5 }.

issues.problem: A horizontal steelDark bar at 1.08 m shows under each pair of monitors. alv_IMG_7207 shows two small round bassinet sockets per panel, about 0.3 m apart, and no bar.
issues.fix: In buildBulkhead (m.bassinet): replace the gRBox(0.3, 0.03, 0.02) bar with two discs: for su of [-0.15, 0.15], add gCyl(0.018, 0.018, 0.01, 12) rotated to face the cabin, at (x+su, 1.08), in { c: '#2a2a2e', r: 0.4 }.

issues.detail: Galley upper units: dark gradient band (lighting cross-area)
issues.problem: The upper standard units go from near-white at the top to dark grey within 0.3 m, so they look frosted and smudged. The real units are uniform brushed aluminium.
issues.fix: Lighting/AO hand-off (12_scene.js AO volume under the ceiling lip). In 10_mono.js, an optional mitigation is a small emissive (e:0.02) on aluDark for the upper bank only.

issues.problem: The counter reads as mid-grey, not the glossy black top.
issues.fix: Darken MONMAT.basalt to about #18171c with r 0.15, or give the welcome counter its own material.

issues.problem: Faint vertical seam in the lower middle flap (carried over). The flap frames are flat, square strips where lalf_133 shows rounded-corner raised frames.
issues.fix: In buildAshWall, replace the four gBox frame strips with a single gRBox(pw + 0.06, 0.91, 0.02, 0.03, 2) frame behind the flap (alu), with the flap at +0.004 in front. Push the flap to F(x, 1.28, 0.01) to cover the body seam.

Do you have a photo of the door-4 or door-5 economy galleys? Their layout follows the seat map, and the brewer detail is taken from SANspotter's door-4 snack-bar photo.
